# ***Media Society Proposal***

&nbsp;

**Academic Year:** 2026–2027&nbsp;

**Proposed by:** Raied Faisal and Eshaal Waseem

**Target Organization:** Pakistan International School Jeddah – English Section (PISJ-ES)&nbsp;

**Proposed Authority:** Student Co-Heads (Male Head & Female Head)&nbsp;

**Administrative Oversight:** Principal & Deputy Head

**Date:** 15th Sep, 2026

## 

## 

## **1\. Executive Summary & Foundational Framework**

### **Vision**

To establish a centralized, synchronized, and professional student media body that manages and executes all digital content, event coverage, and visual identity for Pakistan International School Jeddah – English Section (PISJ-ES). The **Media Society** acts as the official media powerhouse of the institution, replacing fragmented event-by-event media teams with a disciplined, unified student organization.

### **Mission**

To deliver consistent, high-caliber, and ethically grounded visual media coverage across all school events, academic functions, extra-curricular societies, and athletic competitions. The **Media Society** empowers students to cultivate advanced technical capabilities in digital media while strictly upholding institutional values, privacy standards, and administrative protocol.

### **Core Values**

> * **Responsible Representation:** Ensuring every captured photo, recorded video, and designed asset reflects the highest standards of school culture, reputation, and local regulatory requirements.  
> * **Equal Opportunity:** Providing an inclusive platform for dedicated students across all high school grade levels to contribute, collaborate, and excel without arbitrary grade-tier limitations.  
> * **Institutional Support:** Serving as a reliable creative partner to all student bodies, academic departments, and event organizers across the campus.  
> * **Integrity & Accountability:** Maintaining total transparency with school administration and enforcing strict control over device usage and digital media distribution.

## **2\. Institutional Problem Statement & Centralized Solution**

### **The Challenges of the Legacy Model**

In prior academic cycles, individual school events (such as MUN conferences, inter-house debates, sports tournaments, and drama productions) operated under independent, hastily assembled media teams. This decentralized approach created severe operational and administrative difficulties:

> 1. **Unregulated Mobile Phone Misuse:** Lack of a singular authority led to unauthorized personal recordings and unvetted mobile device usage during school hours.  
> 2. **Inconsistent Media Quality:** Fragmented groups produced varying levels of coverage quality, resulting in poor school promotion and lost archival footage.  
> 3. **Administrative Friction:** School leadership and event coordinators had to manage, brief, and hold accountable entirely new media groups for every single function.  
> 4. **Compliance & Privacy Risks:** Absence of a centralized approval protocol increased the risk of improper media distribution.

### **The Centralized Media Society Solution**

The **Media Society** introduces a single, synchronized body with an exclusive official mandate to cover all campus activities.

> * **Singular Administrative Interface:** The Principal and Deputy Head communicate with one structured entity rather than multiple ad-hoc committees.  
> * **Official Media Badging:** Only active members wearing official, school-issued **Media Society** credentials are permitted to operate equipment or capture media during events, immediately solving mobile phone misuse.  
> * **Streamlined Central Storage:** All final assets are deposited into a unified, secure OneDrive cloud system, eliminating local media hoarding on personal devices.

### **Operational Comparison**

| Legacy Team Model (Old System) | Central Media Society Model (New System) |
| :---- | :---- |
| Fragmented, event-specific media teams selected repeatedly throughout the year | One permanent, synchronized central team managing all school events exclusively |
| Unregulated mobile phone usage causing campus distraction and policy breaches | Strict official mandate with Media Credentials worn by authorized members only |
| Lost event media, temporary local storage, and inconsistent visual quality | Unified archival structure hosted centrally on official school OneDrive storage |
| Multiple lines of communication confusing administration and event leads | Single direct line of accountability straight to the Deputy Head and Principal |

## **3\. Scope of Work & Deliverables**

The **Media Society** operates as a full-service internal media body. Rather than dividing members into isolated, rigid sub-teams, all members work collaboratively under the unified scope of the society to execute four main functions:

### **Scope Breakdown**

| Media Service | Key Output & Technical Scope | Primary Application |
| ----- | :---: | :---: |
| **Photography** | Event coverage, formal award shots, candid moments, academic showcases, portraits | School archives, digital publications, yearbooks, news coverage |
| **Videography** | Event highlight reels, full session recordings, interviews, promotional trailers | Official school announcements, assemblies, event recaps, reels |
| **Graphic Design** | Digital announcements, promotional posters, event banners, invitations, social graphics | On-campus displays, official social channels, club promotions, posters, reels |
| **Post-Production** | Video editing, color grading, sound polishing, captioning, visual assets | Final media deliverables submitted for administrative review and publishing |

### **Tools & Software Used**

| Category | Tools & Software |
| :---: | :---: |
| **Photography & Videography** | Camera, mobile phones |
| **Graphic Design** | Canva, Adobe Photoshop |
| **Editing** | CapCut, Adobe Premiere |
| **Feedback** | Google Forms |
| **Documents** | Google Docs |
| **Communication** | WhatsApp |

## **4\. Governance & Administrative Hierarchy**

The **Media Society** enforces a transparent chain of command. The structure eliminates complex middle-management tiers, ensuring direct accountability, rapid communication, and efficient oversight.

### **Chain of Command Structure**

> 1. **Executive Approval Authority:** Principal & Deputy Head  
   * Holds ultimate approval over all policy decisions, media releases, and society operations.  
> 2. **Student Leadership:** Male Head & Female Head  
   * Oversees day-to-day operations, manages member rosters, coordinates event assignments, and conducts content quality checks.  
> 3. **General Membership:** **Media Society** Members  
   * Execute photography, videography, graphic design, and editing tasks on equal footing under co-head coordination.

### **Leadership Responsibilities**

| Leadership Role | Key Operational Responsibilities |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Principal & Deputy Head** | Final sign-off on all media assets prior to publication; policy oversight; emergency intervention. |
| **Male & Female Co-Heads** | Managing event coverage schedules; conducting media reviews; coordinating directly with club leads. |
| **Society Members** | On-field coverage; asset production; graphic drafting; editing execution under co-head guidance. |

## **5\. Strategic Inter-Society Integration & Collaboration**

### **Unified Campus Media Infrastructure**

The **Media Society** is established as the single, exclusive, and official media body for PISJ-ES. Rather than operating in isolation or creating friction with existing student organizations, the **Media Society** serves as a collaborative support engine for all academic departments, extracurricular societies, athletic clubs, and official institutional functions.

By centralizing all technical equipment, media badging, and post-production workflows under one dedicated authority, PISJ-ES eliminates redundant media setups and ensures every campus event receives top-tier, synchronized coverage.

&nbsp;

### **Preservation of Partner Autonomy & Creative Ownership**

A foundational principle of this framework is that partnership with the **Media Society** does not diminish the creative freedom of other student organizations. Partner societies and event committees retain full autonomy over their event concepts, artistic vision, promotional messaging, and reel themes.

&nbsp;

* **Creative Autonomy:** Clubs and societies formulate their unique narrative, select target themes, and propose promotional reel ideas.  
* **Production Execution:** The **Media Society** acts as the expert production arm—handling camera operations, audio capture, lighting, graphic formatting, and post-production editing to bring partner ideas to life with maximum polish.

&nbsp;

### **Non-Exclusive Membership & Multi-Disciplinary Growth**

To encourage holistic student development and prevent institutional silos, membership in the **Media Society** is strictly non-exclusive:

* **Parallel Participation:** Students are explicitly permitted and actively encouraged to hold concurrent memberships or leadership roles in other school societies, debate clubs, sports teams, or MUN committees.  
* **Flexible Scheduling:** Coverage rosters are managed dynamically by Heads to accommodate members' dual responsibilities, ensuring zero conflict between media duties and active participation in partner organizations.

## **6\. Event Lifecycle & Operational Protocols**

To maintain high operational discipline, all event coverage follows a strict 6-step linear lifecycle.

### **The 6-Step Lifecycle**

> 1. **Planning:** Co-heads assign members, verify equipment readiness, and complete the collaborative briefing session.  
> 2. **Coverage:** Badged members capture required media responsibly under institutional guidelines.  
> 3. **One Drive Archiving:** Assets are uploaded to the central school OneDrive directory for permanent storage  
> 4. **Editing:** Post-production members refine photos, construct recap videos, or design required graphics.  
> 5. **Admin Approval:** Assembled media undergoes two-tier verification, ending with explicit sign-off from the Deputy Head or Principal.  
> 6. **Release:** Approved assets are uploaded to social media.

### **Media Storage Protocol**

All raw and edited media files are stored centrally on official school **OneDrive** online storage. Members are strictly prohibited from maintaining permanent local copies on personal devices or personal cloud drives once the official transfer is complete.

## **7\. Institutional Compliance & Zero-Disruption Policy**

### **Zero-Disruption Academic Policy & Compliance**

The primary objective of all students at PISJ-ES is academic excellence. The **Media Society** functions under an uncompromising zero-disruption mandate, ensuring media commitments never interfere with instructional time, examination schedules, or academic focus:

> * **Blackout Periods & Exam Safeguards:** All **Media Society** operations, event coverage, and post-production duties are subject to an absolute operational blackout during mid-term assessments, final examinations, and mock exam cycles. No media assignments will occur during these periods.  
> * **Academic Schedule Protocol:** Coverage duties must **never** conflict with core instructional hours without explicit, advance written approval from the Deputy Head or Principal.&nbsp;  
> * **Academic Eligibility & Monitoring:** Active membership requires students to maintain a satisfactory academic standing. Any member falling below required academic thresholds will have their coverage privileges temporarily suspended until grades stabilize.

### **Two-Tier Administrative Approval Pipeline**

To guarantee complete risk management, institutional brand integrity, and strict adherence to school policies, no media content created by the society may be published, distributed, or released publicly without navigating the formal two-tier approval workflow:

> * **Tier 1: Student Leadership Quality & Compliance Review**  
  * **Technical & Aesthetic Standard Check:** Male and Female Co-Heads perform preliminary inspections on raw/edited media to ensure they are up to quality standards.  
  * **Initial Safety & Policy Audit:** Co-Heads verify that assets align with school decency standards, privacy guidelines, and event guidelines prior to administrative submission.  
> * **Tier 2: Executive Administrative Authorization**  
  * **Final Content & Brand Approval:** The **Deputy Head or Principal** retains final authority over all digital releases, evaluating media for institutional representation, public relations impact, and cultural appropriateness.  
> * **Publishing Release Sign-off:** Only after explicit, documented administrative sign-off are assets transferred to social media teams or external channels for distribution.

## **Conclusion**

The establishment of the **Media Society** transitions PISJ-ES into a structured, modernized, and highly efficient model for school media management. By centralizing talent, eliminating mobile phone misuse through official badging, establishing strict administrative approval gates, and safeguarding student academic hours, this proposal provides an ideal balance between creative student development and institutional governance.

We believe this proposal outlines a strong foundation for the **Media Society** and its role within the school. However, we are fully open to feedback and willing to make adjustments wherever needed. Any edits, suggestions, or changes are greatly appreciated, and we are open-minded to any improvements that may be recommended. We value the perspective of the **Deputy Head and Principal**, and are ready to work collaboratively to ensure that this society operates in a way that best serves PISJ-ES and its community.
